- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 73+), producing exaggerated downward corrections — cap downward moves to 10–15% of prior peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been trending sharply upward for 5+ days, forecast should not continue upward beyond 1–2 standard deviations above mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to recognize reversal — add a slight upward bias to counteract lag.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.5 in last 5 days → model should be more conservative; reduce forecast volatility by 15–20%.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and price is near 70–72, model tends to overcorrect — cap forecast at ±2 points from current mean.
